clue.text: Bury model who puts her oar in ?

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a poser is one who poses, as an artist's model does

explanation.surface: A buried model seems an odd figure, then turns into a meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts their oar in interrupts or intervenes uninvited, which is what an interposer does.

clue.text: Lie snugly in honest leisure :

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: An honest person lounges comfortably at their leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle in comfortably, as if in a nest.

clue.text: Cardinal superiority

explanation.surface: A two-word note about a churchman's rank.
explanation.walkthrough: His Eminence is the title of address for a Roman Catholic cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is styled His Eminence, and the word also means distinction or elevated standing.

clue.text: Musical antithesis of Strauss's "Alpine Symphony"?

parts.note: the opposite of Alpine is flat lowland, and the opposite of a grand symphony is a bare unaccompanied church melody

explanation.surface: A music critic seeks the opposite of Richard Strauss's mountain tone poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Strauss's Alpine Symphony depicts a mountain climb with a huge orchestra; flat country is the plain, and a simple unison liturgical melody is chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian-style unaccompanied liturgical singing is the opposite of a vast orchestral work, and plain is the opposite of Alpine.

clue.text: He manages rising damp in South Africa Road

indicators.note: the damp piece is placed inside the South Africa piece
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: wet means damp

explanation.surface: A building manager deals with rising damp at a South African address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns WET into TEW, which 'in' places within SA, before RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages an estate, household or a ship's catering.

clue.text: But even well-to-do students appear in them

definitions.text: But even well-to-do students appear in them

parts.words: But even well-to-do students appear in them
parts.note: tattered clothes worn by the poor, and also the charity events British students hold, which even rich students join

explanation.surface: Even wealthy students show up in shabby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British university students' charity carnival or week of stunts, as well as tattered clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered old clothing is worn by the poor, and student charity carnivals are attended by all students alike.

clue.text: Produced by a natural outburst of energy

definitions.text: Produced by a natural outburst of energy

parts.words: Produced by a natural outburst of energy
parts.note: an eruption from a mountain is an outburst of the earth's energy, and lava or rock made by it is described by this word

explanation.surface: Something formed by a sudden burst of natural force, like a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks formed from lava come from a mountain erupting, a violent release of the earth's energy.

clue.text: But his goods would not be gratis

definitions.text: But his goods would not be gratis

parts.words: But his goods would not be gratis
parts.note: the merchant's title includes the word for no charge, yet what he sells still costs money; the free refers to the absence of tariffs

explanation.surface: A trader whose title promises freebies still charges for his wares.
explanation.walkthrough: A free trader trades without customs duties or tariffs; 'free' does not mean the goods cost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who supports or practises commerce without tariffs still sells for money.

clue.text: Member with our mail possibly

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a body part alongside their post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' is chain mail, not letters; 'possibly' marks it as one example of the defined thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is one kind of protective metal covering for a soldier.

clue.text: Form opinion of re-styled team ties

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Judging a team's new set of neckties.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-styled' rearranges the eight letters of TEAM and TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To form an opinion of something is to judge or appraise it roughly.

clue.text: Telegram about the strange case of Mr Know-All

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the other

parts.note: to wire is to send a telegram, and a wire is a telegram

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the next word are made odd, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A telegram concerning a curious mystery involving a smart alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns CASE into SEAC, and 'about' puts WIRE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a smug person who pretends to know everything, a smart alec.

clue.text: Is this forest a rural one ?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a woodland counts as countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Dean is an ancient woodland in Gloucestershire, England; a rural dean is a Church of England clergyman overseeing a group of parishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Dean is a named English woodland, and a rural dean is a senior priest supervising a deanery.

clue.text: Have unfavourable opinion of vapid prose maybe

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the ten letters of VAPID PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To think badly of something is to hold an unfavourable view of it.

clue.text: Shoemaker — livery type

explanation.surface: A cobbler dressed in a servant's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The Worshipful Company of Cordwainers is one of the City of London's livery companies (trade guilds), so a member is a 'livery type'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old trade name for a leather-worker making shoes was taken from Cordovan leather, and the guild of that trade is a London livery company.

clue.text: Paradise for 21, given the right circumstances.

definitions.text: Paradise for 21, given the right circumstances

parts.words: Paradise for 21, given the right circumstances
parts.note: 21 across is the Persian poet whose quatrain says a barren place would be heaven enough with bread, wine and his beloved

explanation.surface: A heaven for a certain poet, provided conditions are right.
explanation.walkthrough: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: 'A Book of Verses underneath the Bough, A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread, and Thou Beside me singing in the Wilderness, Oh, Wilderness were Paradise enow!'
explanation.definitionFit: In the famous quatrain, a desolate wasteland becomes heaven given wine, bread, verse and a companion.

clue.text: Abandoned property of French widow

relict is an old word for a widow, one left behind

explanation.surface: Property left behind by a French widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned property' is a noun here: a deserted ship or building.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or building that has been deserted by its owner is abandoned property.

clue.text: You've had your chips when he rakes them in

definitions.text: You've had your chips when he rakes them in

clue.text: Barrel behind the target?
